note: Scripture authority is the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0), bundled as library/data/bible/owb-am-b.json.gz and read offline (owb-am). Every Scripture quotation was re-quoted to it verbatim (founder decision, 2026-11-18: Amharic quotes OWB everywhere), replacing the 1962/2003 UBS wording and the translator-rendered Old Testament verses the first edition carried.

A `mined` row is a verbatim OWB span in that block: the whole verse, the shortest contiguous span carrying the quoted clause, or exact OWB pieces joined with '…' (Matt 25:31-46 as Law elides it, Rom 6:6, 1 Cor 8:9-13, 1 Pet 2:9). Unmarked recitations are quotations too: Matt 6:20, Acts 16:26, Acts 20:35, 'temple of the Holy Ghost' (1 Cor 6:19) and 'that the works of God should be made manifest in him' (John 9:3) now give OWB's words. Several quotations the first notes missed are re-quoted and noted (1 Cor 7:31, 2 Cor 5:7, Phil 3:15, 3:20, Luke 17:4, Rev 7:9-12, 2 Tim 1:3 and others).

Where Law's next words lean on a quoted word, the prose follows OWB or carries a one-time bridge: the talents of Matt 25 are OWB's 'bags of silver', glossed once as the talent (መክሊት) Law argues from; Phil 3:15's 'mature' is bridged once to Law's 'perfect'; 'Raca' / 'Thou fool' (Matt 5:22) are OWB's ‹አንተ ባዶ ራስ› / ‹አንተ ሞኝ› in every back-reference; Matt 18:22 is 'seventy-seven times'. OWB follows the critical text at 1 Cor 7:34 and 1 Cor 6:20; Law argues from neither missing clause, so OWB stands.

`self_rendered` rows (each with a why) are allusions, Law's own prose echoing a verse, and Acts 10:30: OWB has Cornelius praying where the A.V. has him fasting, and Law argues from the fast, so that sentence is rendered from the English (the `critical-text` decision), not kept in the 1962 wording. The old notes numbered blocks across the whole book with no chapter; their allusion rows for chapters 1-15 were mapped to chapter and block, and chapters 16-23 were noted afresh from the text.
